plays: Dwight White tackled Fran Tarkenton in the end zone for a safety, the only points of the first half (2–0).
Franco Harris ran for a 9-yard touchdown early in the third quarter and finished with 158 rushing yards, a Super Bowl record at the time.
Terry Bradshaw hit tight end Larry Brown for a 4-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter to put the game away.
wins.story: Forty-two years after Art Rooney founded the team, the Steelers finally won a championship. The defense was the star: Minnesota managed only 17 rushing yards, and the Vikings' lone touchdown came on a blocked punt.

plays: Lynn Swann made a leaping, juggling 53-yard catch that is still one of the most replayed grabs in Super Bowl history.
Reggie Harrison blocked a Dallas punt out of the end zone for a safety, starting the fourth-quarter comeback.
Bradshaw threw a 64-yard touchdown to Swann and was knocked out of the game on the play; Glen Edwards intercepted a pass in the end zone on the final snap.
wins.story: Trailing 10–7 entering the fourth quarter, Pittsburgh scored 14 straight points and held on. Swann finished with four catches for 161 yards and became the first wide receiver named Super Bowl MVP.

plays: Bradshaw threw for 318 yards and four touchdowns, both Super Bowl records at the time.
John Stallworth turned a short pass into a 75-yard touchdown in the second quarter.
Dallas tight end Jackie Smith dropped a wide-open touchdown pass in the end zone in the third quarter, and Dallas settled for a field goal.
Franco Harris ran 22 yards for a touchdown and Swann caught an 18-yard score to make it 35–17 before Dallas rallied late.
wins.story: A rematch of Super Bowl X between the two best teams of the decade. It made Pittsburgh the first franchise to win three Super Bowls.

plays: The underdog Rams led 19–17 going into the fourth quarter.
Bradshaw found Stallworth deep for a 73-yard touchdown to retake the lead.
Jack Lambert intercepted a Rams pass to stop their last real threat, and Franco Harris added a 1-yard touchdown run.
wins.story: The fourth title in six seasons capped the 1970s dynasty. Bradshaw became the second player, after Bart Starr, to win back-to-back Super Bowl MVP awards.

plays: Ben Roethlisberger scored on a 1-yard quarterback sneak just before halftime.
Willie Parker opened the second half with a 75-yard touchdown run, the longest run in Super Bowl history at the time.
Antwaan Randle El, a former college quarterback, threw a 43-yard touchdown pass to Hines Ward on a trick play.
wins.story: As the AFC's sixth seed, Pittsburgh won three road playoff games just to get there. Jerome Bettis, playing in his hometown of Detroit, retired a champion after the game.

plays: James Harrison intercepted Kurt Warner at the goal line and returned it 100 yards for a touchdown as the first half ended, the longest play in Super Bowl history at the time.
Larry Fitzgerald's 64-yard touchdown gave Arizona a 23–20 lead with under three minutes left.
Roethlisberger drove 78 yards and hit Holmes in the corner of the end zone with 35 seconds left; Holmes kept both toes down for the winning score.
wins.story: Pittsburgh became the first team with six Super Bowl wins. Mike Tomlin, in his second season, was 36 and the youngest head coach to win a Super Bowl.

losses.note: Down 13–0, the Steelers clawed back to 20–17 helped by a surprise onside kick, but Cowboys cornerback Larry Brown intercepted Neil O'Donnell twice to set up Dallas touchdowns.

Green Bay jumped to a 21–3 lead with help from a Nick Collins interception return for a touchdown. Pittsburgh got within 28–25 but couldn't finish. The Packers' QB and head coach that night, Aaron Rodgers and Mike McCarthy, later joined the Steelers.
